messages:
andrew: Quick sync — thinking through a SLO-aware prewarm credit split for Dedicated pools. Goal: let tenants with tighter p50/p90 latency SLOs consume more prewarm headroom while keeping overall cost bounded. Thoughts?

jia: Love the idea. We should keep the decision localized to the operator, not the control plane. Operator already has live view of pool util and warmup backlog.

andrew: Agreed. Two quick constraints: 1) never go negative on global burst budget; 2) soft reserves should be reclaimable if the pool is under pressure.
sarah: Proposal sketch: compute tenant_prewarm_allowance = base_share + sla_multiplier * tenant_demand_score. base_share = pool_headroom * (tenant_quota / total_quota). sla_multiplier derived from SLO weight (0..1).
matt: How do we compute tenant_demand_score? instantaneous QPS vs historical 5m max?
jia: Use exponentially-weighted average of request_rate with a 5m half-life, plus a small signal for recent sudden spikes (max over 30s). That reduces thrash but is reactive enough.

andrew: Example formula I wrote quickly: 

```
# pseudo
base_share = headroom * (quota / total_quota)
demand_factor = 0.5 * ewma_rate + 0.5 * recent_peak_norm
sla_boost = clamp(SLO_weight * 2.0, 0, 3)
allowance = base_share * (1 + sla_boost * demand_factor)
```

Keep allowance capped by per-tenant max_burst_credit.

sarah: For reclaiming: operator should attach a reclaimable tag to soft reserve leases and run a cheap re-eval every 10s. If pool_util > target and there are pending requests from other tenants, evict reclaimable leases in LRU order.
matt: Eviction policy needs to respect tenant fractional guarantees and avoid oscillation — add a cooldown per-tenant (e.g., 60s) after eviction where they can't re-acquire soft headroom fully.
jia: Also important: expose metrics so product teams can see when SLO-weight boosted them. We should emit: prewarm_allowance, prewarm_used, prewarm_reclaimed, sla_boost_factor per tenant.

andrew: Rollout plan: 1) operator implements a feature-flagged code path for allowance calc (no admission change), 2) emit metrics, 3) run canary on a low-risk DC for 24h, 4) enable admission enforcement (deny beyond allowance) with a soft-fail path (queue + fallback to smaller model) for 48h, 5) full enforcement.
sarah: For soft-fail behavior we should prefer graceful degradation: select fallback variants (quantized model or cpu fallback) with slower latency but preserve correctness. Add a route-level policy to opt-out tenants that don't want fallbacks.
matt: Billing question: are prewarm credits billable? I think no — they're operational. Keep billing orthogonal, but mark heavy prewarm borrowers for follow-up sizing conversations. Emit a chargeback metric only for internal ops.
jia: Operator API surface (minimal): 
```
POST /operator/pools/{pool}/prewarm-allowance/eval -> {tenant, allowance}
GET  /operator/pools/{pool}/prewarm-metrics?tenant=... -> timeseries
PATCH /operator/pools/{pool}/prewarm-config -> {global_headroom_pct, max_per_tenant, sla_weights}
```

andrew: Good. Make sure the eval endpoint is idempotent and read-only. No writes to tenant state.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary deployment started for pool:us-west-2-dedicated-1 (version: prewarm-slo-split-v1) :rocket:

andrew: Observability checklist for canary: prewarm_allowance_vs_usage (per-tenant), eviction_rate, post-eviction latency delta, queue depth, fallbacks triggered. Alert if post-eviction p95 rises > 15% for any tenant.
sarah: Edge cases: 1) very small tenants with tiny quotas getting zero allowance — add a min_floor fraction (e.g., 1% of headroom) so they can still burst. 2) Tenants that game SLO weight via config — SLO weight must be auto-derived from observed error/latency SLA breaches, not user-editable.
jia: Implementation note: do the heavy math in the operator control-loop (Go), but keep the formula parametrized and feature flagged. Unit test with synthetic traces for ramp/spike scenarios.
matt: Simulation idea: run a 24h Monte Carlo load sim with mix of steady and bursty tenants, validate that total prewarm spend < budget and that high SLO tenants see <10% cold-start increase.
andrew: Agreed. I'll open an RFC follow-up and include the pseudo-code + metric names + rollout steps. Quick action items: andrew->draft RFC, jia->add metrics to operator, sarah->define SLA_weight derivation, matt->build sim harness.
sarah: One more: add an operator-level knob to disable sla_boost entirely for cost-constrained pools.
andrew: Nice. Thanks all — will post the RFC link here when ready. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary deployed (prewarm-slo-split-v1) to 5 instances, monitoring for 30m.

matt: FYI — I ran a quick local sim; with the min_floor change small tenants no longer starve. Pushed a gist: https://gist.github.com/matt/prewarm-sim-675

andrew: Excellent. RFC incoming.
